newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 17.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - On Friday evening, after four days of discussions, 131 out of 200 members of parliament, including all coalition representatives and half of the Social Democratic Party, voted in favour of the Czech-German Declaration. President Vaclav Havel regards this as a historic achievement for Czech diplomacy.

- In a ministers' meeting yesterday, Health Minister Jan Strasky received the green light for his concept for financing health care. Included in the concept is that, by March 15, Strasky will present to the cabinet a proposal of regulations which will allow physicians to be paid not only for operations, but primarily for the number of registered patients.

- The Finance Minister announced conditions for creating a uniform accounting centre for orderly trade on the capital market. Parties interested in the tender have until the end of April to submit their offers, and the results should be announced in July.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Government aid for farmers in environmentally unfavourable areas must triple to reach approximately six billion crowns, according to Agriculture Minister Josef Lux. The minister plans to present a proposal for this to the cabinet.

- According to experts, the prepared increase in regulated prices will mean that at the beginning of next year, the year-on-year inflation rate will increase by a few points. Bank deposits with steady interest rates with long-term maturity, whose rates at certain banks are currently falling behind inflation, should deteriorate even faster.

PRAVO - The price of shares of Bohemia Sekt on the Prague Stock Exchange has increased since the beginning of the year from 3,200 crowns to 5,600 crowns and to 6,300 on Thursday in the RM-System. Brokers recommend small holders to sell, because the increase is the result of main shareholders taking an interest in obtaining a decisive share.

- The crown recovered quickly from its decline last week, but its further development is still uncertain. On Thursday, the crown decreased by 3.5 percent above parity, and on Friday, trade closed again at approximately +4.5 percent.
